conviction_note: LX is the one Chinese loan-facilitator that grew originations 15.9% QoQ into the crackdown while QFIN cut its book ~29% and XYF's active borrowers fell 75% YoY, so the sequential provision-release that let all three peers post better-than-feared Q2s is the one lever LX does not have, and it has said nothing publicly since 2026-05-25 while the late-June sector funding shock, the 1 Aug 24%-cap disclosure rule and a ~50% July volume collapse all landed.

findings.finding: LexinFintech grew Q1 2026 originations to RMB57.9bn, +15.9% QoQ and +12.2% YoY, while its 90+ day delinquency rose from 3.1% at end-2025 to 3.5% — it was adding volume in the exact quarter Qifu was cutting its loan balance from RMB126bn to under RMB90bn, so LX's credit provisioning peaks in Q2/Q3 rather than releasing.
findings.why_not_priced: Every Q2 print in this group so far has beaten fear on the same mechanism — shrink the book, release provisions, expand margin (XYF net income +23.8% QoQ on revenue -56.3% YoY; FINV profit +1% QoQ; QFIN adjusted EPS beat by 34%). The market is plainly applying that template to the last name in the sector. If it had noticed LX ran the opposite policy, LX would already trade at a visible discount to QFIN and FINV on price-to-book and the ATM options would have a two-sided market; instead the entire chain carries 3,189 contracts of open interest with a put/call OI ratio of 0.37, i.e. call-heavy, and no one has paid for downside at all.
findings.independence: Qifu's Q2 disclosure of its own book contraction and its statement that industry funding conditions worsened after a late-June shock and have not improved: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-qfin-q2-2026-profit-beats-but-revenue-miss-hits-shares-93CH-4876156

findings.finding: Lexin's offline inclusive-financing business — part of the 'ecosystem' segment management said was nearly 50% of Q1 originations — largely halted from mid-2026 as bank funding tightened, and in July 2026 staff at the Wuhan Optics Valley Financial Port office were given a choice of transferring into collections or staying home on local minimum wage.
findings.why_not_priced: This exists only in Chinese-language commentary and in no company filing, no 6-K, no English wire item and no analyst note. The tell that it has not been absorbed is the sell-side: consensus is still 'Buy' with a $3.50 average price target against a $1.18 spot, roughly 200% upside. Coverage that had marked the loss of half the origination mix would not be carrying a target three times the price. A furlough-or-collections ultimatum at a regional office is what a business unit looks like when it stops, not when it slows.
findings.independence: Separate Chinese outlet describing the same July 2026 internal restructuring of Fenqile staff at the Wuhan Optics Valley Financial Port: https://jg-static.eeo.com.cn/article/info?id=8759a385cc114adaa0fc87170973346d

findings.finding: FinVolution told investors on 2026-08-27 that its China loan volume was down roughly 50% in July, and Qifu said funding costs rose about 25bp across July and August with conditions still not improved after the late-June collapse of loan-facilitation platform Juzi Digital triggered a sector confidence and liquidity shock.
findings.why_not_priced: LX last spoke on 2026-05-25 and guided Q2 originations merely 'stable to flat'. Every one of these events post-dates that guidance, so 31 August is the first time LX quantifies any of it. What is not priced is not the sector fact — it is that LX has to restate its own Q3 trajectory from a base that grew rather than shrank, which makes the percentage cut larger than the peers'. If this were priced, LX would not have spent the last month tracking the sector on a similar 20-day drawdown; it would have decoupled downward the way a name with an un-reset base does.
findings.independence: Chinese coverage of the June 2026 Juzi Digital (桔子数科) collapse and the resulting industry confidence crisis, with 5,191 complaints against a single funding bank by 29 June: https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260707A03F3100

findings.finding: The NFRA/PBOC 'one-form' comprehensive financing cost disclosure rule took full effect 1 August 2026 with a hard 24% all-in cap, and it targets exactly LX's 'low headline rate + guarantee fee + service fee' stack; the NFRA had already summoned Fenqile by name on 2026-03-13 as one of five platforms over marketing inducement, opaque fee disclosure and collection practices.
findings.why_not_priced: The rule was known in April, but 1 August was 30 days ago and the Q2 quarter closed before it — so no company in the group has yet reported a full month under it, and LX has never described what its take rate looks like once the fee stack has to be shown as one number under 24%. The regulation is priced; the first quantification of the take-rate compression is not, and it arrives in the guidance section of this print. If the market had a number for it, the $3.50 consensus target would not survive.
findings.independence: Xinhua Economic Information Daily on the 13 March 2026 NFRA summons of Fenqile over high-rate lending and data collection: https://www.jjckb.cn/20260319/06ef2a2bd5774978834b7cde676af513/c.html

findings.finding: Co-founder Yi Wu sold ADSs in the open market on 2026-07-01, cutting his beneficial ownership to 20,196,118 ordinary shares / 6.1%, disclosed in a 13D/A filed 2026-07-06 — an insider reducing at roughly $1.60 into the sector's funding shock.
findings.why_not_priced: A 13D/A on a foreign private issuer with a $194m market cap and no active option market gets essentially no distribution; there is no Form 4 flow for an FPI to make it show up in the insider screens most desks run. It sits against management's own May statement that it had suspended buybacks 'due to ongoing macro uncertainties' with $11m of the $50m authorisation unspent — the company stopped buying and a founder started selling in the same eight weeks.
findings.independence: Company confirmation in the Q1 2026 release that repurchases were suspended with US$11m remaining under the US$50m programme: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/25/3300493/0/en/LexinFintech-Holdings-Ltd-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Unaudited-Financial-Results.html

searched_and_found_nothing: SEC EDGAR browse-edgar, data.sec.gov submissions API and efts full-text search all returned HTTP 403 from this environment, so I could not enumerate LX's 6-K filings directly and relied on indexed copies and wire releases instead
ir.lexinfintech.com press-release index timed out repeatedly; could not confirm the filing list from the company's own site

No Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency notice found for LX despite a $1.18 spot and a $1.10 52-week low — searched for an 8-K/6-K compliance notice and found none, so the listing angle is a risk rather than a finding
No evidence the Fenqile app has been pulled from Chinese app stores; searched specifically for a 下架 action and found only the March 2026 summons

Could not obtain a live, date-stamped Black Cat (heimao) complaint count for August 2026 — the trend is visible (c.80k Oct-2024, 153,832 Jan-2026, >160k Mar-2026) but I could not source a current figure, so I dropped it as a finding
Found no disclosed revenue or profit split for LX's Mexico/Indonesia overseas business, so I could not test whether it offsets China the way FinVolution's does
No Chinese ABS registration suspension found naming Lexin or Shenzhen Fenqile specifically, only a general report that some consumer-finance issuers had registrations suspended under the new rules
No going-private proposal, strategic review, or major-shareholder accumulation found at the $194m market cap
baseline_tension: It agrees with the tape rather than cutting against it — LX is already -11.3% in five sessions and -19.2% in twenty into a 52-week low, which is the weakest part of this call; the offsetting argument is that positioning shows no fear at all (3,189 total contracts, put/call OI 0.37, no two-sided ATM market) and coverage is stale by a factor of three at a $3.50 target, so the drawdown looks like sector beta being passed through rather than anyone having priced LX's specific decision to grow the book while every peer shrank.
